check.q: Brightwater needs VM temp disks and caches encrypted, not just the managed disks. Which option covers them?
options: Server side encryption with platform keys alone
check.why: Encryption at host encrypts temp disks and caches at the host. Server side encryption alone covers managed disks but not temp disks or caches, and firewalls and locks do not encrypt.

lessons.key: Use encryption at host for full VM disk coverage, plan off Azure Disk Encryption, and use Trusted launch for Secure Boot, vTPM and integrity monitoring.

lessons.title: Azure Bastion and just in time VM access
steps: Bastion

**Azure Bastion** is a managed jump host. Admins connect over TLS on port 443 to Bastion, which opens RDP or SSH to the VM's private address, so ports 3389 and 22 never face the internet. It needs a subnet named AzureBastionSubnet of at least /26, except for the free Developer tier.
Bastion SKUs

**Developer** is free for testing. **Basic** reaches peered networks. **Standard** adds native client connections, IP based connections, shareable links and scaling. **Premium** adds **session recording** and private only deployment. SKUs can be upgraded but not downgraded.
Just in time access

**Just in time VM access**, part of Defender for Servers Plan 2, adds deny rules to the VM's NSG or Azure Firewall for management ports. An approved request opens the port only for the requester's IP and only for a limited time, up to three hours by default, then closes it.
Permissions

Requesting access and configuring policies need separate permissions, so Brightwater gives its support staff a custom role that can only request. Defender for Cloud recommends protecting management ports with just in time access.

check.q: Brightwater's auditors want recordings of every admin session to sensitive VMs. Which Bastion SKU does Tomasi need?
check.why: Session recording is a Premium feature. Standard adds native client and shareable links but not recording, and Basic and Developer have fewer features still.

lessons.key: Bastion removes public RDP and SSH, with Premium adding session recording, and just in time access opens management ports briefly for approved requesters.

lessons.title: Azure Arc and onboarding Defender for Servers
steps: Azure Arc

**Azure Arc** brings servers outside Azure under Azure management. The **Connected Machine agent** connects outbound over 443 and registers the server as an Azure resource with tags, RBAC and a managed identity. Azure Policy, Machine Configuration, Defender for Servers, Update Manager and the Azure Monitor Agent then work as on Azure VMs.
Arc details

The agent sends a heartbeat every five minutes, and silent machines show as disconnected. An **Arc Private Link Scope** keeps agent traffic private. AWS and GCP connectors in Defender for Cloud can deploy Arc automatically.
Onboarding Defender for Servers

For Azure VMs, Tomasi turns the **Servers** plan on per subscription in Defender for Cloud. AWS and GCP machines are covered through multicloud connectors, ideally with Arc. On premises servers use Arc, or **direct onboarding** through Defender for Endpoint, which loses Azure Policy and Machine Configuration.
Plan scope

Plan 1 can be enabled or disabled per resource. Plan 2 is enabled at subscription level and can only be disabled per resource. Brightwater's 30 on premises claims servers are onboarded through Arc so they get the full Plan 2 features.

check.q: Brightwater wants Azure Policy and Machine Configuration on its on premises servers as well as Defender for Servers. How should Tomasi onboard them?
options: With direct onboarding through Defender for Endpoint only
With a site to site VPN
check.why: Arc makes the servers Azure resources, so Policy and Machine Configuration apply. Direct onboarding skips those features, and VPNs or Bastion do not register servers with Azure.

lessons.key: Azure Arc makes non Azure servers Azure resources for Policy, Machine Configuration and Defender for Servers, while direct onboarding loses those extras.

lessons.title: Defender for Servers settings and agentless scanning
steps: Plan components

Defender for Servers settings switch components on. **Endpoint protection** deploys Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for EDR. **Vulnerability assessment** uses Defender Vulnerability Management, on by default where Defender for Endpoint runs. Plan 2 adds premium vulnerability features, file integrity monitoring and the OS baseline assessment.
Plan 2 extras
Plan 2 also covers just in time access, the network map, DNS alerts and 500 MB a day of free security data ingestion per machine. The old Log Analytics agent is retired.
Agentless scanning

**Agentless scanning** takes a snapshot of a VM's disks, analyses the copy in the same region in an isolated environment, then deletes it. It finds software, vulnerabilities, plaintext secrets and, with Plan 2, malware, without touching the VM. It comes with Defender CSPM and Defender for Servers Plan 2.
Scanning details

Scans run every 24 hours on running machines and cannot be rescheduled. Disks encrypted with customer managed keys need the scanner granted key access. Brightwater's legacy VM cannot run an agent, so agentless scanning is its only source of vulnerability data.

check.q: A Brightwater VM runs an appliance image where no security agent can be installed. How can Tomasi still find its vulnerabilities and secrets?
options: Defender for Endpoint EDR in block mode
check.why: Agentless scanning reads a snapshot of the disks, so no agent is needed on the VM. Live response, EDR block mode and file integrity monitoring all depend on the Defender for Endpoint sensor running inside the machine.

lessons.key: Defender for Servers settings enable EDR, vulnerability assessment and Plan 2 extras, and agentless scanning reads disk snapshots without touching the VM.

lessons.title: Azure Machine Configuration
steps: Inside the operating system

Azure Policy alone checks Azure resource properties. **Machine Configuration** reaches **inside the guest OS** of Windows and Linux machines, using configuration packages, to audit or enforce settings such as password rules or TLS versions.
Prerequisites

Azure VMs need the machine configuration extension and a system assigned managed identity, deployed at scale with a built in initiative. Arc enabled servers need nothing extra, because the service is built into the Arc agent.
Assignment types

**Audit** only reports compliance. **Apply and monitor** applies a configuration once, then reports drift. **Apply and autocorrect** applies it and fixes drift automatically. The agent re evaluates configurations every 15 minutes.
Security use

Built in policies audit the Windows and Linux security baselines that Defender for Servers Plan 2 reports as OS misconfigurations. Tomasi uses an apply and autocorrect configuration to keep TLS 1.0 disabled on Brightwater's servers, even if someone turns it back on.

check.q: Tomasi wants a Windows setting enforced and automatically put back if an admin changes it. Which Machine Configuration assignment type fits?
check.why: Apply and autocorrect enforces the setting and fixes drift. Audit only reports, apply and monitor applies once and then just reports drift, and disabled does nothing.

lessons.key: Machine Configuration audits or enforces settings inside the guest OS, with apply and autocorrect fixing drift automatically.

lessons.title: Defender for Containers and AKS security
steps: Defender for Containers

**Defender for Containers** covers four areas: **posture** (agentless cluster discovery and the Azure Policy add on, which can deny risky deployments such as privileged containers), **vulnerability assessment** of images in registries and running containers, **runtime threat protection** through a sensor on each node, and agentless scanning of node VMs.
Coverage
AKS needs no connector. EKS and GKE connect through the AWS and GCP connectors, and on premises clusters through Arc. **Gating** can audit or block images that fail vulnerability rules.
AKS identity and API access

**Entra integration** with **Azure RBAC for Kubernetes** controls who can do what in a cluster or namespace. **Disabling local accounts** removes the static admin credential. **Workload identity** lets pods get Entra tokens without secrets. A **private cluster** or authorised IP ranges limit API server exposure.
Inside the cluster

**Network policies** control pod to pod traffic, which is otherwise all allowed. **Pod Security Admission** enforces baseline or restricted pod standards. The Key Vault secrets store driver mounts secrets, and KMS encryption protects Kubernetes secrets at rest. Brightwater blocks privileged containers through the policy add on.

check.q: Brightwater wants every AKS sign in to go through Entra ID and Conditional Access, with no static admin credential left. What should Tomasi do?
options: Enable network policies on the cluster
Disable local accounts with Entra integration
Make the API server a private cluster
check.why: Disabling local accounts removes the static admin credential, so all access goes through Entra and Conditional Access. Network policies and pod security govern workloads, and a private cluster limits network reach but leaves the local account in place.

lessons.key: Defender for Containers covers posture, image scanning and runtime threats, while AKS is secured with Entra and RBAC, no local accounts, network policies and pod security standards.

lessons.title: Container Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps
steps: Registry authentication

**Azure Container Registry** should be accessed with managed identities or service principals for automation and individual Entra sign in for people. The **admin user** is a shared full access account, disabled by default, and should stay off. Repository scoped tokens cover special cases.
Registry authorisation and network

Roles such as AcrPull and AcrPush, or newer repository roles with ABAC conditions, limit what each identity can do. **Private endpoints** need the Premium tier, after which public access can be disabled, with a trusted services bypass for Defender. Defender for Containers scans pushed images.
Container Instances

**Azure Container Instances** can deploy into a delegated subnet with private IPs, use a managed identity to pull images and reach Key Vault, and keep secrets in secure environment variables. Confidential containers run in hardware protected environments.
Container Apps

**Azure Container Apps** offers external or **internal** ingress, IP restrictions, built in authentication with Entra ID, managed identity for registry pulls and Key Vault references for secrets. Brightwater's claims processing jobs run in an internal only Container Apps environment.

check.q: Brightwater's registry still has the admin user enabled for a build script. What should Tomasi do?
options: Rotate the admin password every month
Use a repository scoped token for everyone
Disable it and give the build an identity
Move the registry to the Premium tier
check.why: The admin user is a shared full access credential, so it should be disabled and replaced with a managed identity holding only AcrPush. Rotating keeps a shared credential, a shared token for everyone repeats the problem, and Premium adds private endpoints but not identity hygiene.

lessons.key: Secure ACR with identities instead of the admin user, narrow roles and Premium private endpoints, and use managed identity and private networking for ACI and Container Apps.

lessons.title: Functions, Logic Apps and App Service
steps: Azure Functions

HTTP triggered functions use **access keys**: function keys, host keys and the master key. Keys are shared secrets, not identities, so real caller authentication should use built in authentication with Entra ID or API Management. Functions support access restrictions, private endpoints on suitable plans, managed identities and Key Vault references.
Logic Apps

A Logic App request trigger's callback URL carries a signature and must be treated like a password, regenerated if leaked. Consumption logic apps can require **Entra OAuth** instead and restrict inbound IPs. **Secure inputs and outputs** hide secrets in run history, and anyone who can edit a workflow can use its managed identity.
App Service

Turn on **HTTPS only**, set minimum TLS to 1.2, and disable FTP or require FTPS. **Access restrictions** allow or deny by IP, service tag or subnet, with separate rules for the deployment site. **Private endpoints** remove public inbound access. Built in authentication, managed identity and Key Vault references keep secrets out of config.
Deployment hygiene

Turning off **basic authentication** for FTP and deployment forces Entra based deployment. Defender for App Service detects attacks and dangling DNS. Brightwater's portal now allows inbound traffic only from Azure Front Door.

check.q: Brightwater's App Service still accepts deployments with a shared FTP username and password. What should Tomasi change?
options: Enable HTTPS only and leave FTP as it is
Add access restrictions to the main site
Raise the minimum TLS version to 1.3
check.why: Disabling basic authentication stops shared publishing credentials and forces Entra based deployment. HTTPS, TLS and main site restrictions protect traffic to the app, not the deployment credentials, and the SCM site has its own rules.

lessons.key: Use Entra authentication over keys for Functions, secure Logic App triggers and run history, and harden App Service with HTTPS, restrictions and no basic auth.

lessons.title: Web Application Firewall and API Management protection
steps: Where WAF runs

**Azure Web Application Firewall** runs on **Application Gateway** (regional, with policies per gateway, listener or path) or **Azure Front Door** (at Microsoft's global edge). Managed rule sets and bot protection on Front Door need the Premium tier.
WAF policy

**Managed rules** such as Microsoft's Default Rule Set block SQL injection, cross site scripting and other common attacks using **anomaly scoring**. **Custom rules** run first and can allow or block by IP, country or rate. **Exclusions** stop specific fields causing false positives. **Detection** mode logs, **prevention** mode blocks: start in detection and tune.
API Management policies

**API Management** policies protect back end APIs. **validate-jwt** or the Entra specific token validation policy checks callers' tokens, audiences and claims. **ip-filter**, **rate-limit** and **quota** policies restrict and throttle, and content validation checks request bodies. Subscription keys identify apps but are not strong authentication.
Locking the back end

API Management can call back ends with a **managed identity** or client certificate. The back end should accept traffic only from API Management, through private networking or access restrictions, so callers cannot skip the gateway. Brightwater puts Front Door WAF in front of API Management in front of its claims API.

check.q: Brightwater's claims API must reject calls without a valid Entra token for the right audience. Which API Management policy does that?
options: A WAF custom rule matching on country
check.why: Token validation checks the JWT's signature, audience and claims and returns 401 if they fail. Rate limits throttle, subscription keys identify apps but are not strong authentication, and geo rules filter by location.

lessons.key: WAF on Application Gateway or Front Door blocks web attacks with managed and custom rules, and API Management validates tokens, throttles callers and protects back ends.

modules.title: Manage and monitor security posture
modules.intro: Controls drift and attackers adapt, so posture must be measured and events collected continuously (about 20 to 25 percent of the exam). This module covers Defender for Cloud posture and workload protection across Azure, AWS and GCP, external attack surface discovery, collecting events in Microsoft Sentinel, and setting up Microsoft Security Copilot. Brightwater Insurance runs a small security team, so Tomasi needs these tools to do much of the watching.

lessons.title: Identifying risk with Defender CSPM
steps: Foundational and paid CSPM

**Cloud security posture management (CSPM)** continuously checks resources for misconfigurations. **Foundational CSPM** is free and gives asset inventory, recommendations based on the Microsoft cloud security benchmark, secure score and remediation across Azure, AWS and GCP.
The cloud security graph

**Defender CSPM** is paid, billed per resource. It builds a **cloud security graph** of how resources connect, which powers attack path analysis, cloud security explorer, risk prioritisation and internet exposure analysis.
Attack paths and explorer

**Attack path analysis** shows chains from an entry point, such as an internet exposed VM, to a critical target. It needs agentless scanning on. **Cloud security explorer** runs graph queries such as internet exposed VMs with severe vulnerabilities that can reach storage holding sensitive data. Fixed paths can take up to a day to disappear.
More features

Defender CSPM also covers critical asset protection, data security posture, governance rules, custom recommendations and AI security posture. Tomasi starts each week with Brightwater's attack paths that end at the claims database.

check.q: Tomasi wants to see whether any internet exposed VM could reach Brightwater's claims database through a chain of weaknesses. Which capability shows this?
check.why: Attack path analysis traces chains from exposed entry points to critical targets using the cloud security graph. Secure score and compliance summarise posture, and next hop checks routing for one VM.

lessons.key: Defender CSPM builds a cloud security graph for attack paths, explorer queries and risk prioritisation beyond free foundational CSPM.

lessons.title: Compliance and workload protection plans
steps: Compliance against frameworks

The **regulatory compliance** dashboard maps a standard's controls to recommendations. Azure gets the Microsoft cloud security benchmark by default, AWS adds the AWS foundational practices and GCP its default standard. Extra standards such as PCI DSS or ISO 27001 need a qualifying paid plan and policy rights, and are assigned at the highest useful scope.
Workload protection

CSPM finds weaknesses. **Workload protection plans** detect active attacks and raise **security alerts**. They are enabled per subscription under environment settings, Defender plans, and each plan's settings choose its components.
Plans to know

Plans cover Servers, Storage (activity monitoring, malware scanning, sensitive data detection), Containers, Databases, App Service, Key Vault, Resource Manager (suspicious management operations), APIs and AI services. DNS alerts now come with Servers Plan 2.
Servers plans compared

Both Servers plans include Defender for Endpoint and agent based vulnerability scanning. Plan 2 adds agentless scanning, premium vulnerability management, file integrity monitoring, just in time access and free data ingestion. Brightwater runs Plan 2 on production and Plan 1 on test VMs, set per resource.

check.q: Brightwater wants alerts when someone performs suspicious management operations, such as mass deletions through Azure Resource Manager. Which plan provides them?
check.why: Defender for Resource Manager watches control plane operations for suspicious patterns. Storage watches data access, foundational CSPM checks configuration, and APIs protects published APIs.

lessons.key: Regulatory compliance tracks standards, and workload protection plans for servers, storage, containers, databases and more raise alerts on active attacks.

lessons.title: Connecting AWS, GCP and hybrid environments
steps: Connectors
A **multicloud connector** is an Azure resource that links an AWS account or GCP project to Defender for Cloud. Creating one needs Contributor on the Azure subscription that holds it.
AWS

Onboarding an AWS **management account** creates connectors for every member account, including new ones, through CloudFormation StackSets. A single account covers one. Tomasi chooses regions, a scan interval, the plans and default or least privilege access, then deploys the CloudFormation template or Terraform.
GCP

GCP onboarding covers a project or an organisation. A generated script run in Cloud Shell creates the workload identity pool and service accounts, so Defender for Cloud uses **workload identity federation** rather than stored keys.
Hybrid machines and vulnerability management

On premises and other cloud servers are protected through **Azure Arc**, which connectors can deploy automatically. **Defender Vulnerability Management** for VMs is on by default with Defender for Servers, using the endpoint sensor, and agentless scanning adds snapshot based assessment with Plan 2 or Defender CSPM.

check.q: Brightwater has 15 AWS accounts under one AWS Organization and expects more. How should Tomasi connect them?
options: A single account connector for each account
Connect each account through Azure Arc
A connector in each AWS region
check.why: Management account onboarding uses StackSets to create connectors for all member accounts, including new ones. Single account connectors need manual work for each new account, Arc covers servers rather than accounts, and connectors are not per region.

lessons.key: Multicloud connectors bring AWS and GCP into Defender for Cloud, management account onboarding covers new AWS accounts, and Arc covers hybrid servers.

lessons.title: Defender External Attack Surface Management
steps: The outside in view
**Defender External Attack Surface Management (EASM)** maps what an attacker sees of you from the internet: domains, hosts, IP blocks, certificates and web apps, including ones IT forgot about.
Discovery

Discovery starts from **seeds** such as organisation names, domains, IP blocks and ASNs, but not private addresses. Seeds sit in **discovery groups** with their own schedules, and exclusions stop unrelated assets being added. Many organisations get a prebuilt attack surface to start from.
Inventory and dashboards

Assets are marked **approved**, candidate, dependency, monitor only or requires investigation. Dashboards cover inventory changes, security posture, GDPR compliance, OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25 and CISA known exploited vulnerabilities.
With Defender CSPM

Defender CSPM includes EASM integration without a separate licence, adding internet exposure validation and attack paths that start from internet facing addresses. Tomasi finds an old marketing site on a forgotten Brightwater domain running an outdated, exploitable plugin.

check.q: Brightwater suspects old websites on forgotten domains are still online. Which tool is built to find them?
check.why: EASM discovers internet facing assets from seeds such as domains and organisation names, including forgotten ones. The other tools work on resources you already know about inside Azure.

lessons.key: Defender EASM discovers internet facing assets from seeds and flags exposed vulnerabilities, with integration included in Defender CSPM.

lessons.title: Sentinel workspaces, roles and content hub
steps: Workspaces

**Microsoft Sentinel** runs on a **Log Analytics workspace**. Enabling it needs Contributor on the subscription, and the workspace cannot be moved afterwards. In the Defender portal, one **primary workspace** receives Defender XDR incidents and correlates with them; secondary workspaces can still ingest Defender tables. Keep one workspace unless residency, billing or separation demands more.
Roles

**Reader** views, **Responder** also manages incidents, and **Contributor** also creates rules and installs content. **Playbook Operator** runs playbooks by hand, and **Automation Contributor** is for Sentinel's service account only. Logic App Contributor builds playbooks and Workbook Contributor saves workbooks.
Content hub

The **content hub** installs **solutions**, packages of connectors, rules, hunting queries, workbooks, parsers and playbooks for a product, plus standalone items. Installing turns nothing on: each item must be configured, such as creating rules from templates. Some solutions depend on others.
At Brightwater

Tomasi uses one workspace in the Australia East region, gives the two analysts Responder and Playbook Operator, and installs the Microsoft Entra, Azure Activity and Windows Security Events solutions, then creates rules from their templates.

check.q: Tomasi installs a content hub solution, but no new detections appear. Why?
options: The workspace needs to be moved first
Its rules must be created from the templates
check.why: Installed solutions provide templates, and each rule must be created and enabled. Solutions include rules, connectors and more, workspaces cannot be moved after Sentinel is enabled, and Responders can see rules.

lessons.key: Sentinel runs on a Log Analytics workspace with one primary in the Defender portal, uses layered roles, and content hub solutions provide templates you must enable.

lessons.title: Collecting Azure, Syslog, CEF and Windows events
steps: Microsoft and Azure connectors

API based connectors such as **Microsoft Entra ID** write sign in, audit and risk logs to their own tables, with sign in logs needing P1 or P2. Azure resources use **diagnostic settings**, often deployed with Azure Policy and a remediation task, and Azure Activity lands in AzureActivity.
Syslog and CEF

Appliances send **Syslog** or **CEF** to a Linux forwarder running the Azure Monitor Agent. A **data collection rule (DCR)** sets the forwarder and the minimum log level per facility, and a script configures the daemon to listen on port 514. Data lands in Syslog or CommonSecurityLog. Using the same facility for both duplicates data.
Windows Security events

**Windows Security Events via AMA** uses a DCR to collect from Azure or Arc enabled servers with event sets All, Common, Minimal or custom XPath, and writes to **SecurityEvent**, which most built in rules query.
Windows Event Forwarding

**WEF** sends events from many computers to a collector, where the AMA forwards them into **WindowsEvent**. It avoids installing agents everywhere, but rules expecting SecurityEvent must be adapted. Brightwater uses Security Events via AMA on servers and WEF for branch PCs.

check.q: Brightwater's built in Sentinel rules query SecurityEvent, but events from WEF collectors never match. Why?
options: The DCR level is set too high
The collector needs Security Events via AMA too
check.why: The Windows Forwarded Events connector writes to WindowsEvent, so rules written for SecurityEvent must be adapted or those machines collected with Security Events via AMA directly. WEF keeps event IDs, and the collector setting is not the issue.

lessons.key: Use API and diagnostic settings connectors for Azure, a Linux forwarder for Syslog and CEF, and choose Security Events via AMA or WEF knowing the table each writes to.

lessons.title: Custom tables, automation and retention
steps: Custom tables

Custom tables end in _CL. Text files from servers use **Custom Logs via AMA** into a table with TimeGenerated and RawData. Apps push data through the **Logs Ingestion API** using a DCR with a transformation and an Entra app holding Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the DCR.
Automation rules

**Automation rules** trigger when incidents are created or updated or alerts are created. They change status, severity, owner and tags, add tasks or run playbooks, sequentially by order, and can expire on a set date for temporary suppression.
Playbooks

**Playbooks** are Logic Apps with incident, alert or entity triggers that take actions such as blocking a user or posting to Teams. Logic App Contributor builds them, Playbook Operator runs them by hand, and Sentinel's service account needs permission on the playbook's resource group, granted by an Owner.
Retention

The **analytics tier** keeps data for rules and hunting, 30 days by default and up to two years, with 90 days free for Sentinel solution tables. The **data lake tier** stores data cheaply, with total retention up to 12 years, queried with KQL jobs. Moving a table to the lake stops rules on it, and lowering total retention has a 30 day grace period.

check.q: Brightwater must keep proxy logs for seven years but never runs detection rules on them. Where should Tomasi store them?
options: Analytics tier for two years, then delete
The analytics tier for seven years
check.why: The data lake tier is cheap long term storage, up to 12 years. The analytics tier tops out at two years and costs more, so seven years is not possible there, and advanced hunting keeps 30 days.

lessons.key: Bring custom data in with DCRs and the Logs Ingestion API, automate with automation rules and playbooks, and use the data lake tier for long, cheap retention.

lessons.title: Querying Purview Audit in Defender XDR
steps: The unified audit log

The **unified audit log** records user and admin activity across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Entra ID and more. **Audit (Standard)** is on by default with 180 day retention. **Audit (Premium)** keeps key records for a year, adds custom retention and insights such as **MailItemsAccessed**, and a 10 year add on extends retention.
Audit search in Defender

The **Audit** page in the Defender portal works like Purview's: filter by dates, activities, users and record types, then export. It needs the **Audit Logs** or **View-Only Audit Logs** role, for least privilege rather than Global Administrator.
KQL in advanced hunting

The **CloudAppEvents** table in advanced hunting holds Office 365 and connected app activity, once the Microsoft 365 app connector in Defender for Cloud Apps collects Microsoft 365 activities. Useful columns include the action type, account, admin operation flag, external user flag, IP address and object name.
Scripting

Search-UnifiedAuditLog in Exchange Online PowerShell searches the same log. When a claims manager's mailbox forwards mail outside Brightwater, Tomasi queries CloudAppEvents for new inbox rules by that account in the last week.

check.q: Tomasi wants to query Microsoft 365 user activity with KQL in Defender XDR advanced hunting. Which table should he use, and what must be connected?
options: OfficeActivity with the Azure Activity policy
check.why: CloudAppEvents holds Office 365 activity once the Microsoft 365 app connector collects it. OfficeActivity is a Sentinel table fed by a different connector, AuditLogs covers Entra directory changes, and EmailEvents covers mail delivery only.

lessons.key: Audit search in Defender mirrors Purview Audit, and CloudAppEvents in advanced hunting holds Microsoft 365 activity once the app connector is set up.

lessons.title: Security Copilot workspaces and roles
steps: Workspaces

A **Security Copilot workspace** is created with a unique name that cannot be renamed, a **capacity** of provisioned Security Compute Units (SCUs) with optional overage, and a **data storage location** that cannot be changed later. A capacity serves one workspace at a time. Prompts can be evaluated in the same geography or anywhere with capacity.
Owner settings

Each workspace's owners control capacity, data sharing with Microsoft, file upload permissions and plugins. Audit logging to Purview is set tenant wide by a Security Administrator. Some Microsoft 365 E5 tenants receive an included SCU allowance.
Copilot owner and contributor

**Copilot owners** manage settings, plugins, roles and agents. **Copilot contributors** create sessions, submit prompts and run promptbooks. These are not Entra roles and grant no access to security data: Copilot works on behalf of the user, who still needs, for example, Sentinel Reader to query Sentinel.
Assigning access

Roles are assigned per workspace to users, security groups (recommended), Entra roles or managed identities. Some admin roles, such as Global Administrator and Security Administrator, inherit owner automatically. Tomasi gives contributor to a Brightwater security analysts group rather than handing out Security Administrator.

check.q: A Brightwater analyst is a Copilot contributor but Copilot cannot read Sentinel incidents for her. Why?
options: She also needs a Sentinel role
Her workspace has no SCUs left
check.why: Copilot roles grant no data access, and Copilot uses the user's own permissions, so she needs a role such as Sentinel Reader. Contributors can use plugins, the owner role adds settings rather than data access, and exhausted SCUs would affect all prompts, not just Sentinel.

lessons.key: Security Copilot workspaces fix name and data location at creation, and owner and contributor roles grant no data access, because Copilot uses the user's own permissions.

lessons.title: Copilot plugins and agents
steps: Plugins

**Plugins** connect Security Copilot to products and data. Users manage them from Sources in the prompt bar, and some need per user setup such as choosing a workspace. Owners decide whether preinstalled plugins are available to all users or owners only, and who may add custom plugins for themselves or the whole organisation.
Custom plugins

A custom **Security Copilot plugin** manifest, in YAML or JSON, has a descriptor and skill groups. Skills can call REST APIs described with OpenAPI, run KQL against Sentinel or Defender, or use GPT prompts. Tomasi uploads a plugin that queries Brightwater's claims fraud API.
Microsoft agents

**Agents** run tasks on a trigger or on demand. Setting one up means choosing an identity, ideally a new **Entra Agent ID** with only the permissions granted, rather than an existing user account. The **Phishing Triage Agent** needs Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, and the **Conditional Access Optimization Agent** suggests or creates policies in report only mode.
Security Store agents

The **Security Store** offers partner agents and solutions billed through Azure Marketplace. Getting one needs Contributor or Owner on the billing subscription and Copilot owner or contributor to set it up. If a partner agent reaches Microsoft products, a Global Administrator must approve its permissions before setup works.

check.q: Tomasi buys a partner agent from the Security Store that reads Defender and Entra data, but its Set up button is disabled. What is needed?
options: A Copilot owner must enable the plugin
A new Sentinel workspace is required
check.why: Partner agents that call Microsoft product skills need a Global Administrator to approve their permissions before setup is enabled. Plugin settings, workspaces and subscription ownership do not replace that approval step.

lessons.key: Owners control which plugins users get, custom plugins add skills, and agents should run as Entra Agent IDs, with partner agents needing Global Administrator approval.
